至少得十年前了，那时候的我还是个小学生，对电脑游戏的认知还只有4399。
我在4399上很喜欢玩一种名为“魔塔”的游戏。游戏里精致的像素画风，对我来说简直就是艺术品。其实“魔塔”的本质就是一个数学游戏，放到现在的游戏里算很硬核的了，虽然没有太复杂的公式，但真要认真玩的话，还是得在脑海中推演很长时间的。而传统的“魔塔”游戏几乎都是固定关卡，熟练了自然可以背板，但初见就会显得困难无比。对当时的我来说，一方面是懒得动脑，一方面是时间有限，因此我每次都只会去玩无敌版，也只体会过无双割草的乐趣。
然而当我在4399上发现这款游戏后，事情开始了变化。这款游戏的画风和传统“魔塔”不一样，却同样精致。更新奇的是，这座魔塔里的关卡是完全随机的！对一个小学生来说，完全随机的关卡组成的游戏，简直能玩上一辈子！即使4399上搬运的版本没有无敌版（其实就是由个人修改代码后发布的魔改版本，相当于模组了吧），我也去打了一把，难度比传统的“魔塔”低多了，在没有存档的条件下打到了-20层。
但之后就没法继续玩了。因为我在4399上玩的这个版本，其实只是原作者发布的demo。想要继续玩，就要购买正版游戏。但一个小学生是无法理解demo和正版游戏的概念的，就像中世纪的人无法理解网络的概念一样。于是这款特殊的魔塔游戏就成了我童年的一个遗憾，我也一直没看到游戏里矮人王国最后的结局。
这一等就是近十年。随着阅历的提升，我也了解到要通过Steam等平台购买正版游戏。感谢我的父母，为了我而买了台新电脑。在我还是个小孩时，我以为这款需要花钱买的游戏会很贵。然而真正到购买的时候，我才发现和真正的3A大作相比，它就是一个简简单单的小游戏，不贵，也没有那么神秘。
在一系列机缘巧合之下，这款在Steam上默默无闻的小游戏，成为了一个游戏爱好者了解正版游戏的窗口。这份好评迟到了十年，由当年的那个孩子给出。

Every zone has some mechanic to it that keeps the experience interesting - beating the zones are the few highlight moments you get here. Once you beat the game, it's also possible to grind the final boss for a decent amount of soul stones, which help a ton with any future runs.

Everything else, however, feels very rough around the edges - the story is bland, the sound and music volumes are way too loud and it's very easy to glitch out the game. The mouse inputs don't work most of the time, small mistakes can quickly ruin your progress and grinding soul stones is very boring.

Maze mode is RNG hell; find sword, shield, upgrades, a key and kill a boss. However, sometimes there's no sword, sometimes there's no key and in the final zone, the boss has a 50% chance of being literally unkillable. You can be 10 minutes into a run before realizing that the run was un-winnable from the start, which feels very stupid.

If you're a completionist, you'll need to do some grinding here (a couple story mode runs, some speedrun attempts and 50 maze mode clears), which imo is ok for a bit, but frustrating once the novelty wears off.

DungeonUp, developed by Clewcat Games and published by Plug In Digital, is a compact but surprisingly cerebral dungeon crawler that reframes familiar roguelike conventions through a lens of planning, foresight, and risk management. While it borrows visual and structural cues from classic dungeon adventures, DungeonUp distinguishes itself by slowing the pace and turning nearly every action into a calculated decision. Rather than emphasizing reflexes or chaotic combat, the game asks players to think several steps ahead, making it feel closer to a strategic puzzle experience wrapped in the skin of a roguelike.

The core loop places you in control of a lone knight ascending through procedurally generated dungeon floors filled with monsters, locked doors, traps, keys, and upgrade opportunities. Enemies do not roam or chase you in real time; instead, they occupy fixed positions, transforming encounters into deliberate choices rather than spontaneous reactions. Before engaging in combat, players can usually predict the outcome, allowing them to decide whether a fight is worth the cost. This deterministic approach removes guesswork from individual battles and shifts the challenge toward route planning, resource conservation, and long-term survival.

Dungeon layout and progression are driven heavily by procedural generation, ensuring that no two runs are identical. Each floor presents a new configuration of rooms, corridors, enemies, and keys, requiring players to adapt constantly. Keys are a central mechanic, as doors often block access to upgrades, treasure, or even the exit itself. Deciding which doors to open and which to ignore becomes a meaningful strategic choice, especially when resources are limited. Opening the wrong path too early can leave you underpowered later, while hoarding keys may restrict growth and lead to missed opportunities.

Resource management plays a defining role in the experience. Gold earned from defeated enemies can be spent at altars to improve stats such as health, attack, or defense, but these upgrades are spaced out in a way that rewards patience. Spending too freely early on can result in marginal gains, while saving gold for later floors often leads to more impactful upgrades. This creates a satisfying tension between short-term safety and long-term power, encouraging players to think beyond the current floor and plan for what lies ahead.

As runs progress, the game introduces additional layers through boss encounters and the Soul Stone system. Soul Stones act as a meta-resource earned across runs and can be spent on powerful effects such as resurrection or rare items. This introduces a light rogue-lite element, giving players a sense of persistence and progression even after failure. While this system adds accessibility and flexibility, it can also subtly shift the balance of the game, as accumulated Soul Stones can reduce the severity of mistakes and make certain runs feel more forgiving than intended.

Visually, DungeonUp embraces a clean, retro-inspired pixel art style that prioritizes clarity over spectacle. Floors, enemies, and interactive objects are easy to read at a glance, which is essential in a game built around careful planning. The presentation evokes classic dungeon crawlers without feeling cluttered or outdated, and the restrained visual design keeps attention focused on decision-making rather than visual effects. Sound design and music are similarly understated, providing atmosphere without distracting from the strategic core of the gameplay.

Difficulty scaling is another notable aspect of DungeonUp’s design. Multiple difficulty levels allow players to tailor the experience to their comfort with risk and complexity, with higher settings amplifying the consequences of poor planning and unlucky generation. On these harder modes, the game’s reliance on randomness becomes more apparent, and some runs can feel harsh due to unfavorable layouts or item distribution. While this unpredictability adds replay value, it can occasionally cross the line into frustration when progression feels blocked by factors beyond player control.

Additional modes and features, such as Maze Mode and a level editor with Steam Workshop support, extend the game’s longevity for those who wish to explore beyond standard runs. These options add variety and creative potential, though they are more niche and may not appeal to all players. The main appeal remains the core dungeon ascent, where the balance between knowledge, restraint, and calculated risk defines success.

Ultimately, DungeonUp is a game that rewards patience and thoughtful play above all else. It strips away much of the chaos associated with roguelikes and replaces it with a slower, more deliberate rhythm where every step matters. While its reliance on procedural generation and meta-progression can occasionally undermine its strategic purity, its focus on planning, resource management, and deterministic encounters gives it a distinct identity within the genre. For players who enjoy dungeon crawlers that challenge the mind more than the reflexes, DungeonUp offers a focused and satisfying experience that feels deceptively simple but quietly demanding beneath the surface.

A modern reimagining of Tower of the Sorcerer that fails to understand why Tower of the Sorcerer was designed the way that it was.

Gameplay: 6/10
A solid implementation of TotS' gameplay, the movement is fluid and responsive, sometimes to its disadvantage as you can accidentally walk into a door and use up a key. The game is procedurally generated, in theory providing infinite replayability, but in practice the random nature of the game works at odds with the puzzle-based nature of managing your health. Moreover, the boss battles in the game are ripped wholesale from the original, with the occasional difference. This does result in an instance where one boss is far more difficult due to the mage replacement moves out of position such that you cannot kill the boss. In addition, the game has a very basic settings menu that does not allow changing the volume of the very loud music and sound effects.

Sound Design: 5/10
As mentioned before, there's not much way to alter the volume inside of the game, I had to manually adjust it outside of the game to compensate. The sound effects aren't much to write home about.

Level Design: 0/10
This is where the game suffers the most. It's randomized, that means you could get unlucky and effectively get softlocked because you didn't figure out the most optimal path through an area. Worse, dying results you either restarting, or respawning at the previously defeated boss with the rooms regenerated. TotS had static levels with carefully curated encounters, where trial and error could allow a player to make progress even if they restart from scratch.

Story: N/A
What story there is consists of an excuse plot, much like the original. There's not much here to keep you engaged.

Overall: 4/10
Even discounted, it's not a game I particularly care about. It feels like bad attempt at turning a puzzle game into a roguelike without understanding how the original works.

DungeonUp is a free to play Adobe Flash/AIR browser game that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a fully fledged PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy web developers, because they want your money for a free browser game.  Charging money for something that's free?  Yes, this is a scam. 

And a bad one.  It's a lazy 2D retro pixel trashware "dungeon crawler" themed game, like a really dumbed down version of Rogue/Hack, but with worse graphics somehow (I'd rather be looking at ASCII instead of yet more pixelcrap).  But what should we expect from a free browser game?  Not a price tag, that's for sure. 

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.

There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

Comically, the game was written in Adobe Flash/AIR (I'm not making this up).  Talk about not using the right tools for the job.  Might as well try to bake a cake with a screwdriver.  The extremely poor choice of game engine here is a major contributing factor to the defects with the game.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the game.  But this only happened once, around the same time that trading cards were applied to the game... so this is just card idlers getting their cards and moving on.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.

So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?

Once more we see greedy devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $5 USD, but it's free to play on the web. 

For comparison, the $5 asking price for this game could get you games like "Metro 2033", "Sleeping Dogs" or "The Witcher 2".  So buy any of those on sale, and if you still want to play this, you can play it for free in your web browser. 

Web developers must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free browser game just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Hello, fellow gamers and enthusiasts! I'm Scootaloo, a 19-year-old school-age Pegasus pony, hailing from the icy terrains of HowlStrom. [h2]Embarking on the DungeonUp Journey[/h2]
"DungeonUp" presents a unique blend of roguelike and puzzle gameplay, set in a dynamic, procedurally generated dungeon. Its premise is simple yet captivating: navigate through a labyrinthine dungeon, battle monsters, and unravel puzzles to ascend the depths. This game, in many ways, mirrors my life in HowlStrom, where survival hinges on wit and strategy.

[h3]Game Mechanics: A Mélange of Challenge and Strategy[/h3]
The core gameplay of "DungeonUp" revolves around making strategic choices at every step. As a lover of both puzzles and RPGs, I found this game to be a delightful amalgamation of the two genres. The game requires you to calculate your moves, manage resources like keys and health potions, and choose your battles wisely. It's a refreshing departure from traditional hack-and-slash dungeon crawlers.

[b]Graphics and Aesthetics[/b]
The game sports a charming pixel art style, reminiscent of classic 16-bit games. Each dungeon zone boasts distinct thematic elements, keeping the visuals fresh and engaging. As someone who appreciates the beauty in simplicity, I found the game's visuals to be both nostalgic and pleasing to the eye.

[u]Storyline and World-Building[/u]
"DungeonUp" offers more than just gameplay; it's imbued with a light yet intriguing storyline. The narrative, though not the game's focal point, adds a layer of depth, making the dungeon crawling experience more immersive. The occasional lore and NPC interactions sprinkle bits of storytelling, much like the tales we share in HowlStrom around the fire.

[i]Sound and Music[/i]
The game's soundtrack, with its 8-bit charm, complements the visual aesthetics perfectly. The music enhances the dungeon-crawling experience, though I occasionally muted it for a more serene gaming session. The sound effects are apt and contribute to the overall retro vibe of the game.

DungeonUp: Uma Jornada Épica no Coração das Trevas

Introdução:
Prepare-se para uma jornada épica nas profundezas de um calabouço escuro e traiçoeiro em "DungeonUp". Este desafiador jogo rogue-like é uma homenagem ao clássico "Tower of the Sorcerer". Você assume o papel de um cavaleiro humano que busca escapar de um calabouço profundo, enfrentando monstros temíveis e resolvendo quebra-cabeças intrincados.

Desafio em Cada Passo:
"DungeonUp" é um jogo que exige habilidade e estratégia. À medida que você avança pelas profundezas do calabouço, enfrentará inúmeros desafios. Monstros sedentos de sangue e quebra-cabeças elaborados testarão sua coragem e sagacidade.

Exploração Profunda:
As profundezas do calabouço são vastas e repletas de segredos. A exploração é uma parte fundamental do jogo, pois você busca desvendar os mistérios que envolvem este lugar sombrio.

Visualmente Estimulante:
Os visuais de "DungeonUp" criam uma atmosfera envolvente de escuridão e perigo. Cada andar do calabouço é cuidadosamente projetado para desafiar e surpreender você.

Recomendação:
"DungeonUp" é altamente recomendado para os amantes de jogos desafiadores que apreciam uma mistura de ação, estratégia e quebra-cabeças. Este jogo oferece uma experiência intensa e gratificante à medida que você luta pela sobrevivência nas profundezas do calabouço. Se você está em busca de um desafio que testará suas habilidades de pensamento rápido e estratégia, este é o jogo certo para você. Prepare-se para uma jornada épica, onde cada passo pode ser seu último. "DungeonUp" é uma aventura emocionante no coração das trevas que o manterá envolvido do início ao fim. Enfrente os horrores do calabouço, resolva enigmas mortais e prove que você é digno de escapar deste labirinto mortal. A bravura e a inteligência são suas melhores armas nesta jornada implacável.

DungeonUp, rastgele üretilen zindanlarla dolu bir roguelike oyunudur. Oyuncuların amacı, farklı katları olan bir kuleyi keşfetmek ve zindanları geçmek için mücadele etmektir. Oyun, retro piksel sanatı ve basit, kullanıcı dostu bir arayüz ile sunulur.

Oyunda, bir karakter seçer ve zindanlarda ilerleyerek yaratıklarla savaşırken, hazine ve eşyaları toplamaya çalışırsınız. Zindanların her katı, farklı düşman türleri, tuzaklar ve gizli geçitlerle doludur. Ayrıca, zindanın sonunda, zorlu bir patron sizi bekler.

DungeonUp, oyuncuların rastgele yaratılan zindanlarda yolculuk yaparken farklı yetenekler, eşyalar ve özellikler kazanmalarını sağlar. Oyuncular, her katı bitirdikten sonra ödüller kazanır ve kazanılan ödüller, karakterlerinin gücünü artırmak için kullanılabilir.

Oyun, düşük bütçeli bir indie oyunu olduğu için sınırlı özelliklere ve içeriğe sahip olabilir. Ancak, zindanları ve düşmanları yaratmak için kullanılan rastgele üretim algoritması sayesinde, her oyun oturumu benzersiz bir deneyim sunar.

DungeonUp, oldukça keyifli bir roguelike oyunudur. Retro piksel grafikleri, rastgele üretilen zindanlar ve karakter özelleştirme seçenekleri gibi unsurları sayesinde, oyunculara sürekli değişen ve ilginç bir oynanabilirlik sunar. Eğer roguelike oyunları seviyorsanız, DungeonUp'ın size keyifli bir deneyim sunacağına eminim.

Pretty good little game. You can pretty much figure out the strategy right away, but there are a few little tricks you would never figure out on your own. If you want to know the un-figure-out-able tricks, refer to this guide: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=617950988

This game is a light RPG, puzzle, and adventure mix. Your stats are basic—money, health, attack, and defense—and there are magic items to collect. The puzzle aspect mainly revolves around strategic key usage (unless you’re on easy mode), and the adventure element lets you talk to NPCs who give clues about upcoming challenges.

However, missing a clue about a boss cost me over an hour of progress, which was frustrating. The medium difficulty is challenging enough to be motivating, but after the setback, I wasn’t eager to replay it all, even though the levels regenerate. There’s also a maze mode where you have limited resources and limited visibility of the level, adding to the difficulty.

I’d recommend this game for its concept and fun mechanics. If you don’t make the same mistake I did (engaging a boss without proper knowledge), it’s a solid experience. Considering its price, I can’t thumbs down it. Recommended!

Was ist DungeonUp? Ein Rogue-like RPG welches sehr viel wert auf Taktik und Planung legt, denn hier kommt es nicht darauf an wie gut Ihr in dem Spiel seid sondern welche Gegner Ihr wann besiegt oder wann Ihr einen Heiltrank holt bzw. eine Waffe verstärkt. Dieses andere Gameplay was man vielleicht mit einer Mischung aus Taktikshooter und Autokartenspiel (da Ihr meist Werte vergleicht) beschreiben kann ist etwas frisches neues im Einheitbrei der Rogue-likes und RPGs. Auch zu erwähnen wäre da noch die Schwierigkeit da es selbst auf dem leichtesten Schwierigkeitsgrad oft sehr knifflig ist und Ihr nicht wie in anderen Spielen einfach durch jedes Level laufen könnnt. Vielleicht sollte noch erwähnt werden das Ihr euch wie in einem Strategiespiel jeweils in Vierecken bewegt aber nicht nur eine bestimmte Anzahl an Schritten gehen dürft, die Gegner bewegen sich ausser in Bosskämpfen bzw. wenn Ihr bestimmte Gegner angreift nicht in andere Richtungen. Zum Ende bleibt zu sagen das DungeonUp ein Strategie Rougue-like RPG ist welcher jeder mal ausprobiert haben sollte das es wirklich ein gelungener Mix dieser Genres ist, Daumen hoch.

Franchement, je suis mitigé.
Je suis tombé sur ce jeu par hasard en cherchant à retrouver un vieux jeu indé nommé "Tower of Sorcerer". 
Le jeu avait l'air d'être "inspiré" du dit jeu donc je l'ai acheté (pour le prix, ça se tentait).

En fait, j'hésite entre me le faire rembourser ou le garder parce que quelqu'un a fait sur le workshop de quoi rejouer au vieux jeu indé. 
Car le jeu d'origine, sur les 10 premiers niveaux... 9 sont générés de façon procédurale et donnent des situations absurdes où utiliser une clef bleue (sensé offrir des chemins plus simples au prix d'une clef rare) mène finalement à... exactement les mêmes monstres/objets voir à un chemin pire.
Ou alors souvent des choix de chemin qui sont.... les mêmes en réalité, même nombre de monstres, mêmes items.
Et le 10e étage qui lui n'est pas aléatoire... est une copie exacte de la salle du jeu d'origine à l'exception que le sorcier est devenu une araignée.
Et en regardant les screens des autres joueurs sur des étages bien plus élevés ça ne semble pas changé.
En fait la génération procédurale qui semble ne servir qu'à compenser la flemme des créateurs de créer un vrai level design baisse grandement l'intérêt du jeu.

Finalement j'ai juste eu envie de retélécharger le vrai Tower of Sorcerer même s'il marche moyen sur nos PC actuels.
